subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 34-year-old mountaineer ascends to 4,300 m over 3 days. He has a headache but no dyspnea at rest; pulse oximetry is 86%, arterial PaO2 is 48 mm Hg, PaCO2 is 30 mm Hg, and hemoglobin is 17.6 g/dL. His erythrocyte 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate concentration is elevated compared with his sea-level baseline, and his oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve has shifted.
question: Which of the following best describes the effect of the elevated 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate in this patient?

options.text: It increases hemoglobin oxygen affinity, so less oxygen is delivered to tissues.
It binds deoxyhemoglobin and decreases oxygen affinity, improving unloading of oxygen to tissues.
It binds oxygen directly as a competitive antagonist at the heme iron.
It shifts the dissociation curve to the left and lowers the P50.
It is produced by phosphofructokinase-1 from fructose-1,6-bisphosphate in the liver.

explanation_correct: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate is generated in erythrocytes by the Rapoport-Luebering shunt from 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate via bisphosphoglycerate mutase. It binds the deoxy conformation of hemoglobin, stabilizing the T state and lowering oxygen affinity (right shift with increased P50), which enhances oxygen delivery at altitude; it is also increased in chronic anemia and hypoxia and in pyruvate kinase deficiency.

explanation_incorrect.A: A right shift lowers oxygen affinity, which increases rather than decreases tissue oxygen delivery; factors that raise affinity, such as fetal hemoglobin, carbon monoxide, and alkalosis, shift the curve left.
explanation_incorrect.C: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate binds the central cavity of the hemoglobin tetramer, not the heme iron; oxygen itself binds the heme.
explanation_incorrect.D: The curve shifts to the right and the P50 rises, meaning a higher PaO2 is required for a given saturation.
explanation_incorrect.E: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate arises from 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate in red cells via bisphosphoglycerate mutase and is not produced by phosphofructokinase-1 in the liver.

educationalObjective: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate, produced by the erythrocyte Rapoport-Luebering shunt, binds deoxyhemoglobin and right-shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to improve tissue oxygen delivery.
